podcast.body: This album is viewed by Jay Ferguson as part of an unofficial double album alongside "Navy Blues," due to both being recorded closely together at the same location. Ferguson notably wrote only one new song for this record during that period, reflecting a continuous creative flow between the two albums. "I consider Navy Blues and between the bridges almost a double album because they were done close together at the same place and I only wrote one new song for this new record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was considered a "real tank" in terms of career success and sales, despite receiving a "respectable 3 out of 5 stars" from Rolling Stone. The title is a geographical reference to Sloan's Halifax roots, specifically the Macdonald and McKay bridges in the municipality. "But that was one that totally tanks. Nobody even knows about that one."
